analysis:
The code snippet is a private method that parses a property name string (dot-separated) into an array of strings. It uses StringTokenizer to split the string by "." and adds each token to an ArrayList. Then it calls propName.toArray(new String[propName.size()]). The toArray method is from java.util.List, and the documentation lists two exceptions: ArrayStoreException and NullPointerException.

ArrayStoreException is thrown if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in this list. Here the list contains String objects (since tokenizer.nextToken() returns String). The array is a String array, so String is a supertype of String (same type). Thus no ArrayStoreException can occur.

NullPointerException is thrown if the specified array is null. The argument is new String[propName.size()], which is always non-null. So NullPointerException is avoided.

Therefore, both exceptions are avoided in this calling context.
answer: For the exception ArrayStoreException: its throwing condition is avoided because the list contains only Strings and the array is String[], so the runtime type of the array is a supertype of every element. For NullPointerException: its throwing condition is avoided because the array argument is created with new and is never null.
remark: Both exceptions are avoided; no exception can be triggered in this code.
